body: Of an evening, a war, a meeting. (тянуться, тащиться)
examples: As the evening wore on, people started leaving.
The meeting wore on for another hour.

senses.head: Grate on someone
body: Wear at their patience over time. (действовать на нервы, изматывать)
examples: His voice really wears on me.
The commute started to wear on her.
Twelve-hour shifts wear on you after a while.

entries.pronunciation note: on the particle when time wears on (as the evening wore ON); on the verb when it means irritate (it WEARS on me)
entries.русский: тянуться (о времени); действовать на нервы, изматывать
entries.type: phrasal verb (verb + particle) in sense 1, prepositional verb (verb + preposition) in sense 2
entries.separable: no, either way — in the time sense there is no object at all, and in the irritating sense the object always follows: wears on me, ✗ wears me on.
entries.transitive: either — no object when time wears on, an object after on when something wears on a person
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in both senses: time dragging past (as the evening wore on) and something grinding at a person's patience.
entries.passive: no — sense 1 is objectless, and the prepositional object of sense 2 will not promote: ✗ I am worn on by his voice, ✗ she was being worn on by the commute. Use wear down when you need the passive.

entries.meaning: Use something until it is no longer usable, or tire a person to the same point.
examples: He wore those sneakers out in one season.
The brake pads are worn out.
Wear it out — that's what it's for.
Two hours at the playground wore the kids out.
That trip wore me out.
They stayed a month and wore out their welcome.

senses.head: Use until useless
body: Of shoes, tools, parts. (износить, истрепать)
examples: He wore those sneakers out in one season.
The brake pads are worn out.
Wear it out — that's what it's for.

senses.head: Exhaust someone
body: Leave them with nothing left. (измотать, вымотать)
examples: Two hours at the playground wore the kids out.
That trip wore me out.

senses.head: Wear out your welcome
body: Stay so long that people stop being glad you came. (злоупотребить гостеприимством)
examples: They stayed a month and wore out their welcome.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.separable: yes — wear out the sneakers or wear the sneakers out, and a pronoun must split: wore me out, never ✗ wore out me.
entries.transitive: either — transitive when something wears a thing or a person out, intransitive when the thing itself wears out
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; the participle is fully adjectival after be, which is where learners meet it first: the brake pads are worn out.
entries.passive: yes — those sneakers were worn out in one season, the kids were worn out by two hours at the playground. The idiom resists: ✗ their welcome was worn out.
entries.see also: wear down, wear off, wear away

entries.meaning: Work something into a larger whole — a thread into cloth, a theme into a story — so that it does not look bolted on. Note that when weave means zigzagging through traffic, its past is the regular weaved, not wove.
examples: She wove three separate storylines in without losing the reader.
Try to weave in a reference to the earlier data.
Weave it in near the end so it doesn't interrupt the argument.
The composer wove the folk tune in under the strings.
He weaves personal detail in better than most reporters.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.separable: yes — weave in a reference or weave a reference in, and a pronoun must split: weave it in, never ✗ weave in it.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic, literal with thread and figurative with a theme or a reference.
entries.passive: yes — a reference to the earlier data was woven in, the folk tune was woven in under the strings. Note the participle is woven, not weaved, in this sense.

entries.meaning: Regain something you lost — trust, affection, customers, a title.
examples: It took him two years to win her back.
The airline is trying to win back business travelers.
They won the seat back in the fall.
You can't win them back with a coupon.
She won back the title she lost in 2019.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.separable: yes — win back the customers or win the customers back, and a pronoun must split: win them back, never ✗ win back them.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic: regaining trust, customers, or a title you had lost.
entries.passive: yes — the seat was won back in the fall, the title she lost in 2019 was won back last spring. With a person it is possible but less common: she was won back eventually.

entries.meaning: Prevail in the end, usually after a long contest between two forces or two motives.
examples: Common sense won out in the end.
Curiosity won out and I opened it.
The cheaper design won out over the prettier one.
In the long run, quality usually wins out.
Her stubbornness won out again.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.русский: в итоге победить, взять верх, возобладать
entries.separable: not applicable — there is no object to place. What it beats follows over: won out over the prettier design.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic and intransitive; what it beats goes after over, not into an object slot: won out over the prettier design.
entries.passive: no — no object anywhere, so nothing can be promoted: ✗ the end was won out in, ✗ the prettier one was won out over.

entries.meaning: Bring someone doubtful or hostile around to your side.
examples: She won over the whole committee in ten minutes.
It took a while, but he won them over.
The free samples won us over.
He couldn't win his father-in-law over, no matter what he did.
The second half of the movie won over even the critics.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.русский: склонить на свою сторону, расположить к себе, переубедить
entries.separable: yes — win over the committee or win the committee over, and a pronoun must split: won them over, never ✗ won over them.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic: bringing a doubter around, usually over time.
entries.passive: yes, and it is common — the whole committee was won over in ten minutes, even the critics were won over by the second half.

entries.meaning: Come out successfully after serious difficulty. Americans say pull through, come through, or win out.
examples: The team won through to the final.
She won through despite two injuries.
They won through in the end, but it cost them.
An American would more likely say they pulled through.
He believed decency would win through.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.separable: not applicable — there is no object to place.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic and intransitive; British, where an American says pull through or win out.
entries.passive: no — objectless, so there is nothing to passivize: ✗ the final was won through to.

entries.meaning: Relax after effort, or bring an activity gradually to an end.
examples: I need an hour to wind down after a shift.
The party was winding down by eleven.
They're winding the program down over two years.
The company wound its European operations down in 2019.
Let's wind it down — people are falling asleep.

senses.head: Relax
body: Come down from a working state. (расслабляться, приходить в себя)
examples: I need an hour to wind down after a shift.
The party was winding down by eleven.

senses.head: Bring gradually to an end
body: Of a business, a program, a war. (сворачивать, постепенно прекращать)
examples: They're winding the program down over two years.
The company wound its European operations down in 2019.
Let's wind it down — people are falling asleep.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb — and note the vowel: /waɪnd/, like find, not /wɪnd/ like the weather
entries.separable: yes when there is an object — wind down the program or wind the program down, and a pronoun must split: wind it down, never ✗ wind down it. Of a person relaxing there is no object: I need to wind down.
entries.transitive: either — intransitive when a person or an event winds down, transitive when someone winds an operation down
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in both senses; sense 1 (a person or a party relaxing) is intransitive, sense 2 (closing an operation down) is causative.
entries.passive: restricted — the causative sense passivizes readily (the program is being wound down over two years, the European operations were wound down in 2019); the relaxing sense has no object: ✗ an hour was wound down after the shift.

entries.meaning: End up somewhere you did not plan, bring something to a close, tighten a spring, or get somebody agitated.
examples: We wound up at a diner at two in the morning.
If he keeps this up he'll wind up in court.
She wound up the meeting early.
Let me wind this up — we're out of time.
He wound the old clock up every Sunday.
Sugar winds them up and then they crash.
In London, stop winding him up means stop teasing him.

senses.head: End up somewhere
body: Informal, intransitive, usually with a hint that it was not the plan. (в итоге оказаться, кончить тем, что)
examples: We wound up at a diner at two in the morning.
If he keeps this up he'll wind up in court.

senses.head: Bring to a close
body: Finish a meeting, a speech, a business. (завершить, свернуть)
examples: She wound up the meeting early.
Let me wind this up — we're out of time.

senses.head: Tighten a spring
body: Clocks, watches, toys; the noun windup comes from here. (заводить)
examples: He wound the old clock up every Sunday.

senses.head: Make someone agitated
body: In America mostly in the participle: the kids are all wound up. Deliberately teasing someone — stop winding him up — is British. (взвинтить, раздразнить)
examples: Sugar winds them up and then they crash.
In London, stop winding him up means stop teasing him.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb — the vowel is /waɪnd/, like find
entries.русский: в итоге оказаться; завершить; заводить (часы); взвинтить, раздразнить
entries.separable: yes when there is an object — wind up the meeting or wind the meeting up, and a pronoun must split: wind it up, never ✗ wind up it. In the "end up somewhere" sense there is no object at all.
entries.transitive: either — intransitive in wind up in court, transitive in the other senses
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; sense 1 (wind up in court) is intransitive and close to end up, and sense 4 lives mostly in the adjectival participle after be: the kids are all wound up.
entries.passive: restricted — yes in the transitive senses (the meeting was wound up early, the old clock was wound up every Sunday, the kids were wound up by all that sugar); no in sense 1: ✗ a diner was wound up at.

entries.meaning: Retreat from contact with other people, usually after a shock or a loss.
examples: After the funeral he withdrew into himself for months.
She withdrew into a silence nobody could reach.
The boy withdrew into his own world at school.
He withdraws into work whenever things get hard.
Rather than argue, she withdrew into politeness.
entries.pronunciation note: in a prepositional verb the verb keeps the stress; the preposition stays weak
entries.separable: no — the object always follows the whole phrase, and it is nearly always a reflexive pronoun or a word like silence: withdrew into himself. ✗ withdrew himself into.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic and inchoative: entering a retreat from other people, not occupying one. He was withdrawing into himself is fine.
entries.passive: no — the object after into is reflexive or abstract and will not promote: ✗ himself was withdrawn into, ✗ a silence was withdrawn into by her.

entries.meaning: Send a reply to a letter, an email, or a message.
examples: She never wrote back.
Write me back when you get a chance.
He wrote her back the same night.
I wrote back to the office twice and got nothing.
If they write back, forward it to me.
entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.separable: yes in American English, and the person always goes inside, noun or pronoun alike: write me back, he wrote her back, she wrote her cousin back. ✗ write back me, ✗ she wrote back her cousin. With to the phrase stays whole: write back to the office.
entries.transitive: either — often with no object at all, or with the person written to inside the phrase
entries.verb type: action — dynamic: sending a reply, with or without naming the person replied to.
entries.passive: no — the person sits inside the phrase but resists promotion: ✗ I was written back, ✗ her cousin was written back the same night. Say she got a reply instead.

entries.meaning: Record something in writing — or, in accounting, cut the recorded value of an asset.
examples: Write it down before you forget.
He wrote down the address on the back of a receipt.
She wrote every number down twice.
Nobody wrote anything down, and now nobody remembers.
The bank wrote down the loan by forty percent.

senses.head: Record in writing
body: The everyday sense. (записать)
examples: Write it down before you forget.
He wrote down the address on the back of a receipt.
She wrote every number down twice.
Nobody wrote anything down, and now nobody remembers.

senses.head: Reduce a recorded value
body: Accounting; the noun is a write-down. The opposite is write up. (уценить, списать часть стоимости)
examples: The bank wrote down the loan by forty percent.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.separable: yes — write down the address or write the address down, and a pronoun must split: write it down, never ✗ write down it.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in both the everyday sense and the accounting sense.
entries.passive: yes — the address was written down on the back of a receipt, the loan was written down by forty percent.
entries.see also: take down, write up, write out

entries.meaning: Insert something into a document — in American elections, to vote for a candidate not printed on the ballot — or send a letter to a paper or a station.
examples: Hundreds of people wrote in her name.
He wrote his own name in as a protest.
Write it in under "other."
Listeners wrote in by the thousands.
If you disagree, write in to the paper.

senses.head: Insert into a document
body: Add a name or a clause by hand. The noun write-in is an American election term. (вписать)
examples: Hundreds of people wrote in her name.
He wrote his own name in as a protest.
Write it in under "other."

senses.head: Send a letter to an organization
body: To a newspaper, a station, a company. (написать (в редакцию, на телеканал))
examples: Listeners wrote in by the thousands.
If you disagree, write in to the paper.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.separable: yes when there is an object — write in her name or write her name in, and a pronoun must split: write it in, never ✗ write in it. When it means writing to an organization there is no object: listeners wrote in.
entries.transitive: either — transitive when you insert something, intransitive when you write to an organization
entries.verb type: action — dynamic; sense 1 (inserting a name or a clause) is transitive, sense 2 (writing to a paper or a station) intransitive.
entries.passive: restricted — yes for sense 1: her name was written in on hundreds of ballots, the clause was written in by hand. Sense 2 has no object: ✗ the paper was written in to by listeners.
entries.see also: write down, write out, weave in

entries.meaning: Cancel a debt, record a loss, or decide that someone or something is beyond hope.
examples: The bank wrote off the balance.
We wrote the whole quarter off as a loss.
Don't write him off yet — he's still got a shot.
Critics wrote the album off when it came out.
In Britain he wrote off his car on the motorway; in the US he'd have totaled it.

senses.head: Cancel a debt or record a loss
body: Accounting and tax; the noun is a write-off. (списать)
examples: The bank wrote off the balance.
We wrote the whole quarter off as a loss.

senses.head: Dismiss as hopeless
body: Give up on a person, a team, a project. (поставить крест на, махнуть рукой)
examples: Don't write him off yet — he's still got a shot.
Critics wrote the album off when it came out.

senses.head: Wreck a vehicle
body: British. Americans say total: he totaled the car. (разбить в хлам)
examples: In Britain he wrote off his car on the motorway; in the US he'd have totaled it.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.русский: списать (долг, убыток); поставить крест на; (брит.) разбить машину
entries.separable: yes — write off the debt or write the debt off, and a pronoun must split: write him off, never ✗ write off him.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in all three senses: canceling a debt, giving up on someone, and (British) wrecking a car.
entries.passive: yes — the balance was written off, he was written off too early, the album was written off when it came out.
entries.see also: write down, throw away, take off

entries.meaning: Set something down in full, produce a written document, or remove a character or an heir from a story.
examples: Write the number out in words on the second line.
She wrote out the whole speech by hand.
The doctor wrote out a prescription.
He wrote a check out for the full amount.
They wrote her out of the show after season three.
His father wrote him out of the will.

senses.head: Write in full
body: Spell out what is usually abbreviated or spoken. (написать полностью, прописью)
examples: Write the number out in words on the second line.
She wrote out the whole speech by hand.

senses.head: Produce a written document
body: A check, a prescription, a citation. (выписать)
examples: The doctor wrote out a prescription.
He wrote a check out for the full amount.

senses.head: Write someone out of
body: Remove a character from a script, or a person from a will. (вывести из сюжета, вычеркнуть из завещания)
examples: They wrote her out of the show after season three.
His father wrote him out of the will.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.русский: написать полностью, прописью; выписать (чек, рецепт); вывести (персонажа)
entries.separable: yes — write out the number or write the number out, and a pronoun must split: write it out, never ✗ write out it. In write someone out of something the person always sits inside: wrote her out of the show.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic: setting something down in full, producing a document, or removing a character or an heir.
entries.passive: yes — a prescription was written out, the number should be written out in words, she was written out of the show after season three.
entries.see also: write down, write up, write in

entries.meaning: Turn notes into a full written account — or, in American usage, file a formal report against someone.
examples: I'll write the results up over the weekend.
She wrote up her notes into a full report.
Write it up and send it to legal.
The manager wrote him up for being late three times.
A trooper wrote me up for doing 78.
The auditors wrote the asset up after the appraisal.

senses.head: Produce a full written account
body: The noun is a write-up. (составить отчёт, подробно описать)
examples: I'll write the results up over the weekend.
She wrote up her notes into a full report.
Write it up and send it to legal.

senses.head: Formally report someone
body: American: a disciplinary note at work, or a traffic ticket. (сделать письменный выговор, выписать штраф)
examples: The manager wrote him up for being late three times.
A trooper wrote me up for doing 78.

senses.head: Increase a recorded value
body: Accounting; the opposite of write down. (переоценить в сторону повышения)
examples: The auditors wrote the asset up after the appraisal.

entries.pronunciation note: the particle carries the stress, not the verb
entries.русский: подробно описать, составить отчёт; сделать письменный выговор, выписать штраф
entries.separable: yes — write up the results or write the results up, and a pronoun must split: write it up, never ✗ write up it.
entries.verb type: action — dynamic in all three senses: turning notes into an account, filing a disciplinary report, and revaluing an asset upward.
entries.passive: yes — the results were written up over the weekend, he was written up for being late three times, the asset was written up after the appraisal.
entries.see also: write down, write out, take down
